utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Good morning. Judge Robinson is unable to sit today. He's withheld by other duties, so Judge David and I will set under the rule. I understand that there are some submissions to be made by the parties. Mr. Groome, you want to go first.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. The first witness today was supposed to be MLD17 and there was a matter that I wanted to bring up that relates to both MLD17 and MLD16. The Prosecution wants to inform the Chamber of some matters that affects both of these witnesses. Both of these witnesses are alibi witnesses who are not included in the Defence Rule 67 filings, the alibi filings. Last Wednesday, Judge Robinson ordered the Defence to provide the addresses, dates of birth, and father's name for all their witnesses by Friday last week, and the Prosecution has yet to receive this information from the Defence. Additionally, the Prosecution sent to the Defence on the 21st of January, 2009, a letter requesting an opportunity to interview these two witnesses, and I reminded the Milan Lukic Defence last week in open court about this request and the Prosecution never received a response. This failure to respond to a request from the Prosecution as well as disregard of an order of the Chamber causes several significant problems, in addition to the obvious problem that this failure prevents the Prosecution from conducting even the most rudimentary investigation of who these witnesses are. The problem was compounded in the case of MLD17 because this witness, once again a late-noticed alibi witness who was added in November to the accused's witness list, the terse summary of her statement indicates that she will say she observed Milan Lukic from a window in her home on the day he was allegedly in Belgrade. Not having her address made it impossible to even identify a map for her to indicate where her building is and where she says she saw Milan Lukic. This is especially troubling because we also know that this information is known to the Defence because Victim Witness Services requires this information when scheduling witnesses. I can only conclude that this disregard of the Chamber's order of a few days ago is calculated to obstruct the work of the Prosecution and prevent it from testing the evidence these witnesses will provide today. We will ask the witness under oath to provide this information, although I -- while we've been waiting here, I asked Mr. Alarid to provide this information and he has provided the address now of MLD17, but it's still quite late for us to be able to do anything meaningful with this. So I anticipate that I will be asking the -- or making an application to recall these witnesses at a later time after we've had some reasonable opportunity to do some investigation into their accounts. I would ask the Chamber at this stage to inquire from the Defence as to the reason for its failure to abide by the Chamber's order on such an important issue, ask the Chamber to then consider an appropriate remedy, and to prevent prejudice to the Prosecution's case and further to direct the Defence to fully comply with last week's order by the end of today. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You were also mentioning MLD16. When is MLD16 scheduled to testify?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: She's the second witness on the schedule for this morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Oh, I see. I'm sorry. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, good morning. In response to -- I wouldn't -- in response to the Prosecution's questions to the Court, Your Honour, I wouldn't say that it's a direct issue of disregard. Basically, Your Honour, we scheduled a mission to the region. Mr. Ivetic and I spent two days in Bosnia and we received the clarification from Marie, although I would inform the Court and I did inform Mr. Groome that Ms. Marie O'Leary is no longer with our team. She had prior obligations to the Djordjevic case, and when it came to trial, we had to obviously make concessions. We should hopefully have a new case manager by the end of -- if not next week, given the assignment requirements and the background checks and conflicts checks, that the Registry will be needing to do that. However, Marie did forward the reminder request from the Prosecution to my Blackberry in Bosnia, and we responded as best we could, typing it back, what we had. And basically what I've just given Mr. Groome was what -- basically a reprint and put into the ICTY because apparently -- and we only did it as to the date of birth and father's name, and that's what -- we had actually traveled to the region to meet with these and get as much information as we could for the Prosecution. Of course, we're still doing the due diligence that is, I think, required given the allegations and the problems with the case from prior. You know, again, I stress that we need to provide quality information to the Court given the nature of the Defence case, so that was the reasons why there was the delay, Your Honours. We returned from Bosnia on Sunday and in fact didn't even open Mr. Groome's request until this morning, so that's -- we both picked up a flu in Bosnia, and I got through my fever over the weekend and Dan is in his sort of flu stage right now. So I apologise to Mr. Groome, but it was not an intentional issue, and we're just trying to get as much information as we can ourselves. Right now we're a two-man team, Your Honour, and that's -- that's where we're at. Hopefully we'll have a little bit more support staff by the end of the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I can only urge you to try in the future to comply with your obligations under the rules. For the witnesses of today, I understand the damage has been done, so we will see at the end of cross-examination whether there is a need for the Prosecution to call these witnesses back. I don't think there's anything else we can do under the present circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, we do not object to Mr. Groome's request. Should the need be made, we would, of course, not make any objection to Mr. Groome's request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alarid. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just note that Mr. Alarid, in an e-mail just a few minutes ago, said that we have MLD17's date of birth. We do not have it. If he believes he has given it to us, I'd ask him to give it to us again. But we can find no record of -- we have been given MLD17's date of birth but not MLD16's.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We'll do it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Okay. So are we now ready to proceed to the next witness? Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My apologies. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Your Honour. I would like to raise an issue related to Defence exhibits from our defence list, 24 and 25, which is the transcript of interview with our Defence witness, Mr. Veroljub Zivkovic, conducted by OTP in June of 2008. Since 3rd of November, we have been repeatedly requesting corrections on that transcript from the OTP. During November, we received a revised, due to our opinion partially revised, version of that transcript, but up to now, after three months, we still haven't gotten fully corrected versions. As I said, we repeatedly requested. In the meantime we contacted CLSS related to that issue, and they informed us that they cannot do anything without the Trial Chamber's order. So they need an order to make any correction if we think that they're still existing, and in that interest, firstly, we would like to replace unrevised version of that transcript in the system, which are right now under the numbers 2D05-001 and 2D05-0109, with partially revised transcripts which are under the numbers 2D06-0027 and 2D06-0122. We kindly ask this Honorable Trial Chamber to admit those transcripts as marked for identification and to issue an order related to corrections of those transcripts. I spoke to Mr. Groome last Tuesday, and he told me that he will not object about it. This is contrary. Then I received information from Mr. Cole, so that is our position now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. Would you wish to have this new version to be admitted instead of the old version?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: To be on our list instead of the old version and to request -- to request it be marked for identification, and kindly ask order from the Trial Chamber related to CLSS for additional corrections to that transcript. And we are ready to provide CLSS with a copy of the tape of that interview and with those transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no objection to the Court asking CLSS to review the translations. Just to clarify, Mr. Cepic can correct me if I'm wrong, this relates to -- in the cross-examination of this witness, I played about a five-second portion of the audiotape of the interview, which was then translated contemporaneously by the translators or the interpreters in the booth. Mr. Cepic subsequently would like to introduce the entire transcript, and I advised Mr. Cepic that I would not be introducing it, but I would not oppose any motion by Mr. Cepic if he wanted to make an application to admit those exhibits. So that's what I've agreed to, and hopefully that clarifies some of the details around this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'll be completely -- I'll tell completely our position. We even intended to use that transcript in examination of that witness, but we couldn't because there were a lot of mistakes. There are still a lot of mistakes in that transcript. OTP used just couple seconds, as Mr. Groome said, and even in that small portion of transcript, there were a lot of mistakes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So our position is that in the interests of justice, it's better to have the whole transcript of interview than just a portion or a couple seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Cepic. So then we will have the whole portion of the transcript corrected, and we will accept it, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just for the transcript, those exhibits are on our 65 ter list under the numbers 24 and 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification. So are we ready to call the next witness now? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The witness should be MLD15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: We have to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The witness should MLD15, who's returning, I believe, for the cross-examination of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, MLD16 is a long-time friend of yours; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. From our time in secondary school, we had some joint friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, since you testified in this court on the 14th of January this year, some three weeks ago, how many times have you spoken to MLD16 either in person or on the phone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From what time? Since when?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you testified here in this court on the 14th of January this year, some three weeks ago, how many times have you spoken to MLD16 either in person or on the phone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, since we live in the same town, we ran into each other in the street on one occasion, and she phoned me once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you discuss about this case when you met her on those occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, she mostly talked about her daughters. She takes them to tennis lessons and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you discuss this trial when you were talking to her in the last three weeks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I told her that I was there, and nothing more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you tell her you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the answer relayed to the Court was, "I told her that I was there ..." and now I'm asking you where "there" is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Holland, here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean here at the Tribunal, in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask you about Milan Lukic, and do I have this correct: You believe Milan Lukic to be a wonderful person. You believe Milan Lukic to be a wonderful person; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of what I know of Milan Lukic, that is what I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are you related by family or marriage to Milan Lukic or Sredoje Lukic or their wives; and if the answer's yes, please don't say what the relationship is at this point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm not related to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If we could go into private session briefly, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the first time you met Milan Lukic was at the end of 1990, and when was the last time you saw him in person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was on the 9th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if that's right, as at June 1992 you'd known Milan Lukic for about 18 months.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in that 18-month period or so, how many times did you physically meet with Milan Lukic in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but quite a few times, a number of times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say you met him frequently during that period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the most part, whenever he was in Belgrade, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can you give us some idea? Is it 5, 10, 50 times? How many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ten times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many apartments were you aware that Milan had at that time in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I couldn't really tell you. I don't know how many apartments he had. I don't know whether he had an apartment at all, whether it belonged to him, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go to Milan's apartment in Belgrade in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I went to an apartment, but I don't know whether it was Milan's apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the address that you went to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the name of the street and the house number, but it was at Bezanijska Kosa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Milan Lukic's occupation in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you. I don't know what his occupation was at that time. I knew that he was an athlete, and I know that we discussed that topic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know what his occupation was in June of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you want to conclude that answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, our acquaintance was based on discussions about sports, having fun, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw him ten times and you don't know what his occupation was. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when and where Milan Lukic met MLD16?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall the first time, but I know that we were always together, hanging out in the same crowd, and it was probably during one of those ten times when we were together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's your evidence you can't remember the specific occasion when Milan Lukic and MLD16 met for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, no. I can't remember when the first time was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you related to MLD16?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times have you met Milan's sister, Draginja, who lives in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps two or three times in my entire life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw or spoke with her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I gave the statement to the lawyers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that last year, 2008, you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when I gave the statement to the Defence lawyers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that Draginja has been your contact person about your evidence for Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does she live in the Bezanijska Kosa district of Belgrade, the district that you mentioned previously?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know where she lives. Possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does her husband work for the MUP in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you spoken with Milan Lukic while he's been in the Detention Centre here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two or three times.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your answer, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. He contacted me using e-mail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you saying you've been in e-mail correspondence with Milan Lukic while he's been in custody?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's not what came on the B/C/S channel.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We can hardly hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Can you speak in the microphone, please, sir, because the interpreters have difficulties hearing you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, are you saying that you've been in e-mail correspondence with Milan Lukic while he's been in custody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no e-mails.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The transcript shows that you said that Milan Lukic contacted you using e-mail. What do you say about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We spoke on the phone. No e-mails were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the last time you spoke on the phone with Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that was last year prior to the giving of my statement to the lawyers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you about the time of day that you received the phone call from Milan Lukic in June of 1992, and the question is: At what time of the day did Milan Lukic contact you by phone on the 7th of June, as you say, at your apartment in Belgrade? Morning, afternoon? When was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was around mid-day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this at the same apartment you'd grown up in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If we could go into private session briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this Mijet restaurant, is this where you say that you saw Milan Lukic two days after the surprise party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, two days after the engagement party that I'd prepared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what day of the week was this initial phone call from Milan to you that we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday? What day was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall the day. I remember the date because of the engagement. It was the 7th of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter thinks she heard "July."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you repeat the date, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you referring to the billiard room? We -- I remember, actually, the date because it was the engagement party. That was the 7th of June, and we met at the billiards room on the 9th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Cole -- Mr. Cole, I'm sorry to interrupt you. Why is this ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Cole. I was going to ask you how much time you still need, because we trying to plan the hearing as the videolink witness is lined up. If I give you until 11.00, would that be sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have necessarily because of the nature of this cross-examination some questions. I can reduce them, but can I ask that perhaps 11.15, bearing in mind of nature of this witness, and I'll tailor it to finish then or before then if at all possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Make it 11.10, and then we'll have the break, and then we'll have the next witness after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, very well, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, who was at home with you when you received the call from Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there with my girlfriend of the time, actually, the mother of my son.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, if we could go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you received this phone call from Milan Lukic at about noon on the 7th of June, 1992, what was the purpose of his call?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just a regular call. It was customary as we were wont to do whenever he was in Belgrade. So I took the opportunity to invite him to the party that I was throwing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of the party you were throwing?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're in open session, so I would ask for page 21, line 8, to be redacted accordingly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, had Milan Lukic met your girlfriend before the time of the phone call?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he had, in late 1990 already in Zurich, and from that time it is also possible that he saw her a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the phone call, did you tell Milan the other persons that would be at the surprise party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was a surprise party. I didn't. This was a place of our usual get-togethers, of us, the young people from Zemun. We met there almost daily.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this was a surprise party for your girlfriend, wasn't it? You had invited the other persons --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how long before the surprise party had you contacted the others to invite them along? Was it a week before, two weeks? How long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was a place where we -- actually, our hang-out, where we were every evening, so that there was no need for me to invite anyone specifically. All my friends would be there every evening, regularly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So didn't you have to make a reservation for a table so that you could make sure you had the facility for the surprise engagement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no need because we were regulars there. There was always a table reserved for us, practically, there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how do we spell the name of the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: M-a-c-a.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was one of the persons that you invited to take part in this surprise party your good friend, MLD16?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and she was also a good friend of my, let me say, wife's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So who were the persons present at this table who were to take part in this surprise engagement party, besides yourself and MLD16?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This information was in closed session during the direct examination. I would ask that we go into private session as well for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that at the point that Milan Lukic arrived at the restaurant you were unaware of any bad feelings or friction between him and MLD16?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, I was aware because Milan was always teasing her because of the high heels that she wore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, your testimony on the last occasion when you were here is that you had to take MLD16 home because of some confrontation or some problem with Milan Lukic at the restaurant; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were no direct problems of any kind. It's just that she got up and went away because he was joking at her expense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how long had they both been together in the restaurant before you took her home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know, a minute, two, three, or five. Actually, the moment he appeared, she got up because she knew that he would probably be cracking jokes at her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that point had you given your girlfriend the engagement ring and proposed marriage to her, at the time that MLD16 got up to go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So why did you take MLD16 home and not someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were good friends, and I just thought that it was the right thing to do. I felt a need to do that because she had sat at my table, and I think that it was moral to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was the occasion where you had proposed marriage to your girlfriend and given her a ring. Isn't it a bit odd that you're leaving, taking somebody else home? Couldn't somebody else have taken her home? Couldn't she have got a taxi? Isn't it all a bit strange?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. It isn't, because we were great friends and socialised daily.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She didn't have far to go home, did she?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zemun is not a big town. No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She could have walked or got a taxi easily, couldn't she?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it is not that near. At that time she didn't exactly have taxi fare, so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you took her home and then you returned to the restaurant where everybody was continuing with the celebration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you pay for the drinks, the alcohol, that evening because it was a special occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. It probably was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember what Milan Lukic was drinking that evening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not specifically on that occasion, but I know that as a rule he would have juice to drink whenever we met.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He also drank alcohol, though, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never saw him drink alcohol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Milan Lukic offer to leave the restaurant rather than MLD16 when there was a problem between them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably, but -- knowing him, certainly, but she wanted to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you specifically remember him offering to leave rather than her, or is it something you say you would expect him to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's something I would expect him to do. I'm not sure -- I do not remember with precision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the names of the other people that were there with you celebrating that evening, did you give all their names to members of the Defence team for Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember. This was a place frequented by many young people, and everyone knew everyone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, listen carefully. You gave us the names of some people who were with you at the restaurant that evening. Did you give those names to the Defence lawyers for Milan Lukic; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the Defence team ask you for the names of the other persons who were with you there that evening at the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think they did. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that evening at the restaurant, Milan had the opportunity to speak to everybody else at your table. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really don't know how well he knew the others, but I do know that he came there at my invitation. I cannot remember now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Milan Lukic ask you anything about a city in Serbia called Novi Pazar that evening at the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear him mention it to any of the other persons at the restaurant that evening, that is, the city of Novi Pazar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when was the very first time you knew that you might be a witness for Milan Lukic in this trial? I mean, who contacted you or whom did you contact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My first contact was Milan's nephew, Milojica, or cousin, I'm not sure; anyway, his uncle's son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first hear from a member of the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In November or December, I believe, last year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the members of the Defence team that you met with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This attorney-at-law whom I know as Danny, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that Mr. Ivetic in the courtroom you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many meetings have you had with Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two, I think. Once in Belgrade and also here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So who else was present besides Mr. Ivetic during the meetings you had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in the company of someone else --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreter did not hear the rest of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you repeat the names of the persons that were present during the interviews, that is, in addition to Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the name. He was with someone else. There was someone else escorting him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was Draginja also present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. She received us as ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't understand that answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, I saw her there. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at page 15 of the transcript you said that you gave a statement to the lawyers last year, 2008. Now, do you remember that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually sign a written statement that they took from you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I did, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, where was it that you were when the statement was taken from you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At Bezanijska Kosa in an apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So have I got this right: Mr. Ivetic was present and Draginja. Who else was present at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Another person from here, from the Tribunal at The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that Jelena Rasic or Radomir Rasic, one of those two persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This was a man who I think oversaw everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how many pages was this statement that you -- that you signed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know whether there was any statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Cole. Are you looking at the time? Can you wind up, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, MLD15, think about it. Did you make this written statement and sign it? That's something you'd remember, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that there was no statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you think there was no statement. Is there a possibility that you signed one? Would you accept that, a possibility you did sign a statement on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, asked --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It does exist, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Can you answer the question, Witness. Can you please answer the question, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I think you've just agreed that, thinking about it, you did make and sign a written statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That misstates the evidence, Your Honours. He clearly was answering the question, "Is there a possibility?"

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I would ask that counsel not interrupt and try and instruct the witness as to how to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm entitled to make objections, especially when counsel is overstepping the bounds of what is permitted in this court in misstating the evidence on record. And I object -- I would object strenuously to the Prosecutor trying to intimidate us from making our -- from asserting our rights that we have under the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Cole, can you try to state the evidence more accurately, please, and wind up, because we are running out of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's just be clear about it, MLD15. During the questions about whether you made this written statement or not in relation to these proceedings, you didn't say categorically yes or no, but recorded in the transcript at page 30, line 3, it records that you accepted that it does exist, that is, a statement. Now, the question I'm putting to you: Is the situation now that you accept that you did make and sign a written statement in the presence of Mr. Ivetic and others?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection; compound question; asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Can you answer the question, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I hear the question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'll repeat it from the transcript: "Now, the question I'm putting to you: Is the situation now that you accept that you did make and sign a written statement in the presence of Mr. Ivetic and others?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not a written statement. I cannot recall that. I signed some kind of a paper, but I do not think that that was a written statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you think it was that you signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think Mr. Ivetic is power of attorney to the effect that he can take a statement from me or something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll just now put the Prosecution case in a couple of questions to finish off with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Cole, we gave you until 10 past. We are five minutes beyond it. Just one more question and then we have to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: MLD15, I'm going to put it to you that your evidence is not worthy of any credit and it has been created after the event specifically to provide Milan Lukic with a false alibi. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just three or four questions, Your Honour. I don't know if you want to do it now or after the break.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I would prefer you to do it now because we have to break in order to make the videolink for the witness. Does the tape allow to us go on for a bit? Okay. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. MLD15, when we met in Belgrade the first time, do you recall if the other person in the room with us spoke Serbian or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that that person did not speak Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall if I represented to you from what country he came or hailed from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember. I think that he was a foreigner.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall helping me with a witness information sheet required by the Tribunal for your testimony here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could that be the document that Mr. Cole keeps asking you about here that you mentioned filling out with me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Now I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, MLD15, for your testimony. On behalf of the Defence of Milan Lukic, I wish to thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. MLD15, this brings your evidence to an end. Thank you for coming to The Hague and for giving this evidence. We are now going to adjourn for 20 minutes in order to allow us to make the necessary arrangements for the next witness, who is a videolink witness. Did you want to say something, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your microphone wasn't on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. We shall go into private session because I understood that there is a matter that you wish to raise with this Chamber, so we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 4th day of February, 2009, at 8.50 a.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.55 a.m.,
